root.name: French Defense: Winawer Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Bb4

overview: Black pins the c3 knight. After 4.e5 c5 5.a3 Bxc3+ 6.bxc3 Ne7 White gets the bishop pair and a kingside space advantage, and Black has a damaged-pawn-structure target on the queenside plus the c4 square. White attacks on the kingside (Qg4 hitting g7), Black counters on the queenside and the dark squares. Strategically unbalanced and tense, with a great deal of theory.

white_ideas.idea: Qg4 to hit g7 and h8, then h4-h5 and a kingside attack with the bishop pair
Hold the c3 pawns and play Bd3, Ne2, and f4 or Nf3 with space

black_ideas.idea: Attack the c3 and d4 pawns with ...c5, ...Qc7, ...Nbc6 and ...c4
Close the position with ...c4 to make White's bishop a bad one, and defend g7 with ...O-O or ...Qc7

typical_structures.structure: French chain with White doubled c-pawns on b-c files and Black pawn on c5 and ...c4 lock

character.notes: Known as the sharpest French: g7 attack, doubled pawns, unbalanced play; Sharp.

gambit.notes: The g7 pawn is exchanged or defended; no material is truly given in the main line.

soundness.notes: Sound; a main weapon of Korchnoi and others.

structure.notes: d4/e5 against d5/e6 locks the centre in the main line; Closed, though Delayed Exchange is more open.

level.notes: Heavy theory and sharp lines that must be known; Advanced.

sublines_that_differ.name: Delayed Exchange 4.exd5
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. exd5
sublines_that_differ.how: Quiet, symmetric and Semi-open; Black has an easy game.

character.reason: The best-known sharp French line with g7 attacks and opposing wing play.

gambit.reason: No material given in the main line.

structure.reason: The d4/e5 chain locks the centre after 4.e5 c5.

plans.reason: White's doubled c-pawns, the bishop pair and the g7 attack.
